ours.finding: Codex is the only conductor with native thread status, mid-turn steer, and provider allowance routing. The Grok bridge implements interrupt-and-resume on the same session and explicitly lacks Codex allowance routing. Claude is a bounded headless launch and is missing native thread status, mid-turn steer, and allowance routing. Plimsoll setup wires telemetry for Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Codex; it does not execute those models.

omnara.finding: Provider configs accept OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages, with default paths and auth kinds for each. Callers bring an endpoint and credential, so OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Bedrock-Anthropic, and an Ollama server that speaks one of those wires fit the same resolver. A hosted credential provisioner exists in the supplement. No fourth wire format is accepted by validation.

rows.name: durable agent state and crash recovery

ours.finding: Codex resume checks the native thread id and rebuilds bookkeeping from a full readback, failing closed on a mismatch. Inbox state is a local SQLite hub with explicit recovery instructions. Memory retention replays a journal after interruption and refuses withheld ids. There is no single committed agent-event kernel spanning providers.

omnara.finding: Agent inputs are stored before they become timeline events. Expired runtime-lock recovery is required to lock the agent row before the runtime row. Worker and execution-store tests cover reclaiming an unstarted turn and a failed abandoned context. The machine daemon can disconnect without deleting the agent. This audit did not execute those tests.

ours.finding: The Codex control plane exposes turn start, mid-flight steer, and interrupt over the native app-server. Grok steering is interrupt-then-resume of the same session. Claude has no mid-turn steer. Continuation is a provider thread resume, not a shared delivery queue.

omnara.finding: Content inputs are queued or steering; interaction responses, cancels, and config changes use immediate delivery. Steering is admitted at the next model call, ahead of the queue, and can cancel open questions. Stop cancels the current turn and leaves the agent in place. Config changes apply on the next model call without a new agent id.

ours.finding: Inbox grants cover assignment read, discovery, and leased messages. The launch bus sends one bounded work packet to Codex, Grok, or Claude and keeps a launch receipt. Fleet routing sends one native tool call to an enrolled machine. That is coordination of separate runtimes, not a parent tool that spawns a clean-context child and later reads its timeline.

omnara.finding: spawn_agent, read_agent, send_agent_message, stop_agent, and list_agents are reserved tools. A subagent starts with a clean context, runs in the background, and returns its id immediately. Parent messages do not stop the child's current model call. stop_agent can idle the child or archive it and its own children. Profile and self keys select the child configuration.

ours.finding: Each machine is enrolled by SSH alias plus owner, home, and instance id. fleet_call routes one native operation; credentials, browsers, and process sessions stay on the target. Memory is not replicated by enrollment. Capacity is per host, and one physical desktop still has one focus.

omnara.finding: A BYO machine runs omnarad outbound; the agent stays in the control plane. Org-level machines become usable through project grants and per-agent bindings that carry cwd and environment. The same machine id can be shared. Releasing a BYO binding detaches it and does not delete the computer.

ours.finding: The coordination tree includes a local Tart/VNC actuator for a directly owned VM. Inspected BORG source has no Blaxel, Daytona, Modal, or Unikraft provider, and no idempotent cloud-sandbox allocate/wake/delete API.

omnara.finding: Pool providers are Blaxel, Daytona, Modal, and Unikraft. Provision is idempotent by installation and machine id, must be recorded before the external side effect, and must not leave two live sandboxes for one machine. Wake and delete are retry-safe. Idle pool machines are deleted; BYO machines are not.

ours.finding: A dedicated Chrome CDP bridge exposes session, tab, navigate, snapshot, screenshot, click, and type tools, with private profiles omitted from results. macOS UI tools use open, osascript, and screencapture and report permissions only after a native action. One physical desktop cannot take independent simultaneous focus. Desktop control still needs OS permission grants.

omnara.finding: Built-in web_search and web_fetch reach the public web. web_fetch refuses localhost and private networks. Shell and file tools run on an attached machine, so a browser can be driven only by whatever that machine's shell can launch. The reserved tool catalog has no owned browser session or native desktop click/type tool.

ours.finding: The connector is an authenticated MCP gateway for files, processes, jobs, browser, UI, SSH, and credential handles. Memory ships MCP servers and session hooks. Skill support found in the connector is a directory discovery hint under the Codex profile, not a versioned skill grant. External product MCPs are owner-setup recipes, not bundled servers.

omnara.finding: Agent configs declare HTTP MCP servers with bearer or OAuth secrets, per-tool enablement, and permission modes. The runtime discovers tools, caches catalogs, and can run a stateless streamable HTTP handler. skill is a built-in tool with its own grant and revision store. tool_search loads deferred tools.

ours.finding: Public memory recall embeds with nomic-embed-text and searches a Qdrant collection filtered by user and optional agent, with expiry skips. The fast path returns raw cosine similarity and can order differently from mem0's BM25 and entity fusion. The installed memory-runtime authority gate declines until an out-of-band trust config exists, and that gate is absent from the public BORG memory tree. Memory is documented as recall, not the source of truth.

omnara.finding: Searches for semantic memory, Graphiti, vector stores, and embeddings in Omnara Go and docs found embedding-model ids in provider discovery and no cross-session fact store. Durable agent timelines and context checkpoints are conversation state for one agent, covered under C02.

ours.finding: The public graph feed scrolls Qdrant into scoped Graphiti episodes and is default-off; only canary mode may write while the live flag is off. Scope keys are deterministic hashes. The installed graph adapter fails open to ordinary mem0 recall, marks graph evidence derived_unverified, and reads a scope registry it does not write.

omnara.finding: Omnara's concepts page lists organizations, projects, machines, model providers, skills, secrets, and agents. It does not list a temporal graph. The embedding search that covered Go sources found no episode store or provenance-bearing recall API.

ours.finding: Installed retention can tombstone, decay, or retire points and can withhold ids across an interrupted journal replay. Dream consolidation is an owner-run script; historical schedules are not installed. Fresh installs disable grammar-shim training capture. Public memory tests cover ingest dedupe and dream safety. This is a recall-maintenance pipeline, and the retention module describes itself as marker-oriented.

omnara.finding: Projects, cron triggers, and similar records soft-delete, and secret payloads are encrypted per version. Inspected source shows resource lifecycle deletion, not capture consolidation or semantic forgetting. Self-host docs invite querying Postgres history for training sets, which retains content rather than forgetting it.

ours.finding: Training source includes dataset builders, a held-out exam, and a promotion canary that treats schema validity as the question rather than JSON syntax. The supplement card for the shipped 4B graph adapter says its predecessor failed the real-pipeline canary at 1 of 25 episodes, and that this clean retrain has not been canaried. Adapters are inactive by default. Weight tensors were not in the packet or the supplement file list, so the cards cannot be checked against local weight bytes here.

omnara.finding: An Ollama-compatible endpoint is a model-provider target under C01. Searches of Omnara source and docs found no LoRA training chain, held-out extraction exam, or promotion canary.

rows.name: human operator dashboard and streaming interaction

ours.finding: Codex exposes a per-thread notification stream. The supplement contains an Inbox hub web UI. Plimsoll serves a localhost collector dashboard for usage and outcomes. The public BORG site is a machine planner and install guide. None of these is a multi-user agent conversation console.

omnara.finding: The web app launches agents from a profile, builder, or YAML, streams model deltas with writeSSEFrame, and exposes Stop in the composer. Waiting inputs are visible above the composer. Config-change dividers are documented as API-only in the dashboard so far.

rows.name: team identity, project boundaries and RBAC

ours.finding: An installation has one owner and scoped agent identities. Default agent actions are assignment read, discovery publish/search, and message read/send. Enrolling another machine does not share Inbox records or memory. There is no org/project role matrix for multiple human operators.

omnara.finding: Principals are users, org API keys, and machine daemons. Org roles are owner, admin, and member. Project roles are admin, developer, operator, and viewer, with explicit action implications for secrets, agents, and machines. Launch-only users can start a profile and cannot edit Builder or YAML.

rows.name: human approvals, tool permissions and secrets isolation

ours.finding: Credential handles store provider metadata and hand the agent to a native login; they do not hold secrets. The Codex conductor defaults threads to sandbox danger-full-access and approvalPolicy never, and it denies an approval prompt if one appears anyway. That is isolation by refusal of interactive approval, not a human permission gate. Capture filters and scoped memory grants are a separate boundary.

omnara.finding: Each tool permission is always_allow, always_ask, or always_deny, with schema-checked parameters. ask_question pauses for a person, and steering can cancel an open interaction. Secret payloads are encrypted with org, secret, and version associated data. Compose defaults allow insecure local development, including empty encryption keys until the operator sets them.

ours.finding: Memory capture is hooked into Codex, Claude, and Grok sessions. Plimsoll hooks spool when the local ledger is busy and drain about every five seconds. Inbox delivers leased messages. Dream and graph feed schedules are owner-operated. n8n is an external recipe. No product cron trigger was found in inspected BORG services.

omnara.finding: Cron triggers store an expression, timezone, message template, delivery mode, and idempotency key, and claim due fires. Event webhook deliveries are queued from the compiled agent config. Slack launches one agent per thread or DM from a profile and requires a public HTTPS origin when self-hosted.

rows.name: capacity-aware fleet admission and work ownership

ours.finding: Machine admission fails closed on unknown, stale, unreachable, hot, or memory-saturated observations and on unknown or stale work claims. Local-OS observation uses load per core and memory percent. Fleet-context collectors are owner-built; the installer does not deploy them, and missing observations stay unknown. Live fleet health was left to the lead.

omnara.finding: Workers claim agent work, machines report lifecycle and connection state, and projects have resource limits including active cron triggers. A command waits until the daemon is online or the machine can be woken. Inspected code does not admit work by host load, memory pressure, or a cross-machine claim ledger.

ours.finding: Eligible Codex lanes rank by remaining allowance percent, then reset time, then active turns. Grok and Claude are marked missing provider allowance routing. A launch receipt is not completed work. This audit did not read live account balances.

omnara.finding: Searches for allowance and subscription in Omnara hit max-output token windows and web-search rate limits, which are request shaping, not seat failover. Hosted credential provisioning issues a provider secret for an org. No source was found that moves a running agent from an exhausted subscription account to another included account.

ours.finding: The local collector records tokens, cache reads, model, session, and cost for Claude, Codex, Grok, and Gemini, and local reports stay useful without the hosted service. Hook events that miss a busy ledger are spooled after suppression. Hosted rollups exist, and billing defaults to disabled with no accepted live charge mode. Proof scripts were not executed.

omnara.finding: Model-call rows sum input, cache read, cache write, output, and reasoning tokens, and they sum provider_reported_cost_usd when the provider sent it. Usage still resolves after the configured model is soft-deleted and can include profile subagents to a depth of 64. Cost coverage is whatever the provider reported; there is no separate local harness ledger for tools Omnara did not call.

rows.name: shipped outcome linkage and value measurement

ours.finding: Sessions join pull requests by hashed branch, head sha, or merge sha, and the join can require fetched checks before an unknown-check outcome. Linkage hashes normalized GitHub remotes so raw branch and remote strings stay local. Rework signals include revert and reopen. The collector README treats tokens per merged PR as the product question. This audit did not run the proof suite.

omnara.finding: Searches for pull-request and merged-outcome linkage in Omnara docs and Go found release-tool GitHub URLs and module paths, not a [private session] join. Queryable Postgres is documented as a place an operator could build that analysis.

rows.name: privacy suppression and selective data collection

ours.finding: Metadata mode strips raw prompt, output, and tool content and records a suppression receipt. Spool files pass through the same pre-write suppression. Training-pair capture defaults off, and published adapter cards describe identifier scrubbing before training. The installed graph helper defaults a scope file under one operator home; that path is a portability leak and is omitted here.

omnara.finding: Secrets are encrypted and granted, web_fetch blocks private networks, and MCP auth uses secret ids rather than inline tokens in the documented config. The agent timeline stores prompts, tool calls, and artifacts for the operator by design. That is tenant isolation of a full transcript, not selective suppression of content.

rows.name: idempotency, audit receipts and acceptance evidence

ours.finding: Router admission can persist a status receipt without starting a native process. The launch bus keeps launch receipts that are explicitly not completed work. Inbox mutation request ids are idempotency keys and acknowledgements require the delivery lease. Plimsoll's proof command is a JSON checks binder. None of those proofs were run in this audit.

omnara.finding: Orgs, projects, cron triggers, and agent inputs take idempotency keys, and a reused key for a different resource is a conflict. Sandbox provision and wake must be safe to retry after an ambiguous failure. CI workflows and an OpenAPI compatibility allowlist are in the supplement. There is no single release-evidence binder comparable to Plimsoll proof.

ours.finding: Install is documented and verified for Apple Silicon macOS and pulls local Qdrant, FalkorDB, Ollama, and pinned models into a private home. Linux and Intel artifacts are pinned with native installation acceptance still pending. Windows is unsupported by the installer. Each home owns its data and does not join the author's fleet.

omnara.finding: Self-host is Docker Compose with published images or a local build, Apache-2.0, and a console on port 8000. The stack includes Postgres, Valkey, and blob storage. Compose turns insecure development defaults on unless overridden. Production setup is delegated to the self-hosting guide.

rows.name: public API/SDK, documentation and contribution readiness

ours.finding: BORG publishes MIT code, three papers, a component catalog, an install guide, and a static planner, plus a verify workflow in the supplement. Its HTTP surfaces are an installation-local conductor and Inbox, not a versioned multi-tenant public API. Plimsoll's collector is a public CLI package. Plimsoll Cloud is a private repo and is not approved for paid production.

omnara.finding: The HTTP API is OpenAPI under /api/v1, with a CLI, a TypeScript SDK, and a large docs tree for agents, machines, events, and auth. Supplement CI covers the repo, live tests, CLI, SDK, cluster, and daemon release. Contribution rules are in CONTRIBUTING.md. Generated OpenAPI Go in the supplement is a build artifact, not an independent contract.

axes.name: managed execution
axes.reason: Omnara has one Postgres-backed agent kernel with steering, cancel, subagents, and disposable sandboxes. Our Codex conductor steers and interrupts a native thread, and Grok can interrupt-resume, but Claude cannot, and recovery is split across conductor bookkeeping, Inbox, and memory journals.

axes.name: collective memory
axes.reason: BORG and the installed memory runtime implement scoped vector recall, a default-off temporal graph, and retention markers, with explicit non-authority and unverified graph evidence. Omnara keeps durable per-agent transcripts and has no shared semantic store in the inspected source. The Omnara axis score is 1 because those transcripts are reusable history, not because a memory product was found.

axes.name: fleet operations
axes.reason: Our router fails closed on stale capacity and claims and ranks Codex lanes by remaining allowance, while machine tools stay identity-pinned. Omnara's pools, outbound daemons, grants, and RBAC are a real multi-machine product and do not admit by host pressure or subscription balance. Live fleet health was not measured.

axes.name: delivery economics
axes.reason: Plimsoll joins suppressed local usage to merged pull requests and checks. Omnara sums provider-reported tokens and cost on its own model calls and does not link those calls to a shipped outcome. Hosted Plimsoll billing is disabled by default, so the economics score stays at the local collector.

axes.name: product readiness
axes.reason: Omnara ships an Apache-2.0 API, SDK, dashboard, RBAC, and Compose install, with insecure dev defaults called out. Our stack is a capable Apple Silicon install with benched adapters, asymmetric conductors, a private cloud that cannot charge in live mode, and Linux install acceptance still pending.

recommendations.title: Adopt Omnara's queued, steering, and immediate input kernel for every conductor
recommendations.risk: A second event log can diverge from native Codex thread ids unless resume readback stays the authority for provider state.

recommendations.title: Add an optional idempotent sandbox provider beside BYO fleet machines
recommendations.risk: Cloud sandbox credentials and idle deletion must stay out of the local memory home, and a replaced provider resource must not leave two live VMs.

recommendations.title: Replace the Codex conductor's default never-approve posture with explicit tool permission modes
recommendations.risk: Unattended lanes will stall if always_ask becomes the default without a bounded operator timeout and a recorded denial.

recommendations.title: Offer Plimsoll outcome linkage as an Omnara export that never stores raw prompts
recommendations.risk: Joining Omnara agent ids to GitHub shas on the wrong repo hash would attribute cost to the wrong pull request.

recommendations.title: Expose scoped non-authoritative recall and retention as an optional Omnara MCP
recommendations.risk: If agents treat recalled facts as instructions, the memory layer becomes a second authority. The public graph feed is default-off for that reason.

recommendations.title: Publish the fail-closed capacity admission result for operators who run Omnara workers on their own hosts
recommendations.risk: Omnara pool sandboxes do not have a stable OS load signal, so a Codex-lane ranker must not be copied onto provider capacity it cannot observe.

recommendations.title: Leave benched extraction adapters out of both request paths
recommendations.risk: Promoting the 4B graph adapter on exam JSON scores would repeat the canary failure the cards already record.

limitations: No integration tests, proof suites, or live Omnara, BORG, memory, or Plimsoll processes were run. Test files are coverage evidence only.
BORG runtime and fleet health were left to the lead, so operational scores stay at most 4.

The packet filter omitted conductor implementation, adapter cards, Inbox web UI, and some Omnara CI and hosted-credential files. Those were read from public-supplement at the same pinned revisions. Adapter weight tensors were in neither tree.
memory-runtime is the selected installed source and is not pinned in SOURCE-STATE.json. authority.py is not in the public BORG memory snapshot.
Plimsoll and plimsoll-cloud are working-tree snapshots and may include uncommitted changes. No deployment was inspected.
Absence findings name the search. They are not claims that an uninspected path is empty.
A prior memory query returned unrelated candidate notes and was not used as authority.
Upstream bd 1.2.2 is not installed on this host. The canonical bead [internal work reference] was taken from the fleet job spec and was not mutated.
